subject: Request: SLA remediation credit & exec approval needed
messages:
From: Patrick O'Neil <patrick@astropayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service incidents: request for SLA remediation and credits

Marissa —

Thanks for fielding a post-mortem yesterday. Over the last seven days we've observed repeated latency spikes and two short outages on the payments ingestion endpoint (region us-west). Our engineers traced the impact to kernel-level throttling on a host pool you were running that day; that caused 3–4 minute tail-latency events multiple times and one 22-minute partial outage on 2026-03-03.

Per our contract (SLA section), those incidents put us below the 99.9% uptime commitment for the billing month. The outages caused blocked authorizations on our side and a handful of settlement delays — we estimate direct customer impact and ops cost of ~$18k for that week.

We'd like to request what other vendors call a "service credit" for the impacted month and ask that Redwood provide either: (a) one month of platform credit equivalent to our monthly committed spend, or (b) a prorated usage credit equal to 20% of our March invoice plus a written assurance of improved routing. Also looking for a timeline for remediation and confirmation of additional safeguards (e.g., cross-pool redundancy, throttling mitigations).

I've attached our incident timeline and sample logs for your SREs. Please let me know next steps; we need an answer before our finance team closes the March invoice cycle.

— Patrick O'Neil
Head of Integrations, AstroPayments Inc.
patrick@astropayments.com
Attachment: incident_report_Q1-2026.pdf (pdf, 1.3MB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Patrick O'Neil <patrick@astropayments.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.ops@astropayments.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service incidents: request for SLA remediation and credits

Team — looping you both in for an exec decision. Summary: AstroPayments hit repeated tail-latency and a 22-min partial outage week of 2026-03-01. They are requesting either (A) one free month (full committed spend) or (B) 20% prorated credit for March. They need an answer before their finance cycle closes (end of next week).

SRE follow-up so far: we confirmed the kernel throttling incident, applied a hotfix to the affected pool, and enabled a temporary cross-pool failover for the customer. Ops will push a permanent mitigation this sprint. I've attached the incident report we exchanged.

Recommendation (my read): offer a limited concession to preserve the relationship and reduce churn risk. Proposed concession to present to the customer for immediate resolution: 
- 25% credit on March usage invoice up to one month of committed spend;
- Formal SLA amendment documenting detection/mitigation steps plus a rollback-freeze window;
- 90-day service review with dedicated SRE contacts and weekly health reports.

This needs executive sign-off per our concession policy (anything >20% credit or free-month equivalents must be approved). Rishi — any objections on commercial side? Evelyn — can you sign off if we cap at 25% + the operational commitments above?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Attachment: SLA_Amendment_v1.docx (docx, 45KB)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Patrick O'Neil <patrick@astropayments.com>
Date: Fri, 6 Mar 2026 08:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service incidents: request for SLA remediation and credits

Quick thoughts — thanks for the context, Marissa. I agree we should avoid a full free-month concession unless there's a legal obligation; that sets a risky precedent. 25% credit is within the range I can justify but ask that we add a conditional: customer must sign the SLA amendment and commit to a three-month rolling review cadence (so we don't leave this open-ended).

One more ask from finance: if we provide >20%, apply it as on-account credit (not an invoice refund) and cap cumulative concessions for this account at one month's committed spend. That keeps bookkeeping tidy.

If Evelyn approves, I recommend the message to the customer be: express regret, detail fixes, offer 25% March credit applied as on-account credit, attach the SLA amendment for signature, and request confirmation they will accept the SRE weekly reports for the next quarter.

— Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
rishi@redwood.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Patrick O'Neil <patrick@astropayments.com>, Olivia Chen <olivia.ops@astropayments.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2026 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Approval: Confirmed concession and conditions

Marissa / Rishi — I've reviewed the incident packet and the proposed commercial remediation. Approve the concession with the following guardrails: 

1) Offer 25% credit on March usage applied as an on-account credit (not a cash refund). 
2) Cap total concession at one month of their committed spend. 
3) Require signed SLA amendment (attached) before credits are applied.
4) Require AstroPayments to accept the weekly SRE health reports for 90 days and an operational debrief at 30/60/90 days.

Rationale: preserves the commercial relationship while protecting revenue and forcing mutual operational commitments. Marissa — please send the customer-facing note, attach SLA_Amendment_v1.docx, and confirm when Finance will post the credit. Copy Legal only if they request redlines.

Evelyn Hart
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
evelyn@redwood.com
--
